subject: Executive petition: multi-year rate shelter + renewal protection for HavenHealth
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: multi-year rate shelter + renewal protection for HavenHealth

Team —

Quick summary: HavenHealth (prospect -> committed pilot) is asking for a 3-year agreement with an initial committed ARR of $1.2M and an explicit rate shelter: fix per-token rates for year 1 and 2, with a max annual uplift cap of 7% on year-over-year list price increases, plus a renewal protection clause that preserves unit economics for any SKU migration for up to two renewals.

Why this matters: They are a strategic healthcare customer (large footprint across three states) and procurement has signaled that multi-year price certainty + renewal guardrails are mandatory for any enterprise procurement committee approval. The alternative is losing them to a competitor offering a longer-term price lock.

Ask: Exec approval to offer a three-year term with the following non-standard terms:
- Price shelter: lock current hosted inference per-token rate for 24 months
- Uplift cap: max 7% annual uplift on list price after year 2 for years 3+
- Renewal protection: if customer moves to a different SKU / instance class due to performance needs, we will honor an effective price parity adjustment for up to two renewals (limits to be negotiated)

Impact: Estimated immediate ARR commit $1.2M; modeled gross margin compression ~4.2% in year 1/2 (see attached pricing model). Risks: longer-term revenue upside constrained if market prices fall, small increases in capacity management complexity.

Attachments: HavenHealth_pricing_model_v3.xlsx (pricing model + margin waterfall) and a proposed term sheet draft (HavenHealth_MAAP_Proposed_Terms.pdf).

I recommend we approve on an exception basis with the condition that legal finalizes the renewal protection language and finance signs off on the modeled margin impact. Please advise — priority is to get procurement's signature by 11/12.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive — Healthcare
Redwood Inference
Phone: 415-555-0183

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear summary. High-level reaction: I support making a limited concession for strategic accounts, especially in healthcare where procurement committees favor multi-year certainty. Two immediate asks before I’ll greenlight escalation to Execs:
1) Can you capture the worst-case margin erosion over the full three years and the payback breakeven if they exercise more capacity than committed? (I need a one-slide bullet I can pass to SVP)
2) Confirm the non-negotiables: is the uplift cap absolute (no carveouts) or do we reserve the right to make index-based adjustments for cloud costs?

If we can get those answers today I’ll route this to the deal desk + execs for a final yes. Also loop in CS to confirm support model for SKU migrations (cc-ing Lauren for legal language).

Marissa
Head of Sales, Enterprise

Subject: Re: Request: multi-year rate shelter + renewal protection for HavenHealth

Dylan / Marissa —

I reviewed the workbook. Quick notes:
- Modeled revenue: $1.2M year 1 committed; expected usage overages could raise total ARR to $1.35M at current run-rate (we've put a conservative 10% overage assumption in the sheet).
- Margin impact: gross margin compression of ~4.2% in years 1-2 under the locked rates; by year 3 the uplift cap (7%) reduces margin erosion to ~2.6% compared to baseline list increases.
- Break-even: if overage revenue >20% of committed, the model returns to neutral by year 2.

Questions for legal / deal: what exactly does "renewal protection" mean operationally? Do we define it as: if SKU changes within the same feature parity, we map legacy effective unit price for two renewals only (no credits for retroactive usage). That keeps risk bounded.

I attached a redlined pricing schedule and a short finance memo. Recommend approval only if legal accepts the two-renewal cap and we add an explicit cloud-cost passthrough carveout for extraordinary (>15%) increases in hardware/cloud index.

After reviewing the finance memo and legal's suggested language (Lauren, thanks for the quick turnaround), I approve the following limited exception:
